cases.exposure_context_quote: A 60-year-old woman was found unconscious on July 6, 2025 (Day 0) following intentional ingestion of approximately 300 mL (15 g) of avermectin in a suicide attempt.
cases.agent_quote: following intentional ingestion of approximately 300 mL (15 g) of avermectin in a suicide attempt
cases.circumstance: Intentional ingestion in a suicide attempt; found by family about 2 hours after ingestion; no co-ingestion reported.

symptoms.quote: A 60-year-old woman was found unconscious on July 6, 2025 (Day 0)
Shortly after admission, she developed anuria (urine output <100 mL/24h) with progressive elevation of serum creatinine (Scr), peaking at 256 μmol/L.
Physical examination revealed deep coma with anisocoria (pupil sizes 1.5 and 2.5 mm).
vital signs were as follows: temperature 36.0 °C, pulse 84 beats/min, respiratory rate 18 breaths/min, and blood pressure 77/47 mmHg

cases.time_to_care: Found by family members about 2 hours after ingestion and admitted to the intensive care unit

labs.name: serum creatinine (peak)
labs.quote: she developed anuria (urine output <100 mL/24h) with progressive elevation of serum creatinine (Scr), peaking at 256 μmol/L.

labs.name: thrombocytopenia, schistocytes, LDH
labs.value: anemia, severe thrombocytopenia, elevated schistocyte, and markedly increased lactate dehydrogenase (LDH)
labs.quote: Laboratory evaluation at admission revealed anemia, severe thrombocytopenia, elevated schistocyte, and markedly increased lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) (Table 1).

labs.name: terminal complement complex C5b-9
labs.quote: Complement testing demonstrated markedly elevated terminal complement complex (C5b-9) levels, indicating ongoing complement activation.

labs.name: renal biopsy
labs.quote: Histopathology revealed TMA-like lesions predominantly in glomeruli, including capillary loop occlusion, ischemic alterations, and red blood cell stasis in the Bowman’s space.

treatment.name: gastric lavage, intravenous fluid resuscitation, endotracheal intubation
treatment.quote: She was discovered by family members about 2 hours after ingestion and admitted to the intensive care unit, where gastric lavage, intravenous fluid resuscitation, and endotracheal intubation were performed.

treatment.name: hemoperfusion and CRRT
treatment.quote: Despite 4 days of hemoperfusion for toxin clearance and continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) for acute kidney injury (AKI), there was no improvement in consciousness or renal function.

treatment.name: eculizumab (complement inhibition)
treatment.quote: The patient subsequently received complement inhibition therapy with eculizumab during the disease course.

cases.icu_admission: Yes (admitted to the intensive care unit on Day 0)
cases.outcome: Hematologic abnormalities resolved and renal function recovered with discontinuation of dialysis; renal function stable without relapse at follow-up on March 30, 2026
cases.outcome_quote: At follow-up on March 30, 2026, the patient’s renal function remained stable without evidence of relapse, supporting the possibility that short-term complement inhibition may be sufficient in toxin-triggered TMA, although longer-term observation is warranted.
cases.sequelae: None reported at follow-up; renal function stable without relapse
cases.notes: First reported case of TMA following avermectin poisoning; TTP and STEC-HUS excluded; ITGA2B variant of uncertain significance identified.
